description: Make Instagram Reels and feed ads from one product photo: get a 9:16 clip and a square still to crop 4:5, with no shoot and the cost shown first.
h1: AI Instagram Ads From the Product Photos You Already Have
lead: Need Reels and feed ads without booking a shoot? One product photo gives you a 9:16 UGC-style clip and a square still ready for Instagram.
card: 9:16 Reels clips and square product images.
intro: Instagram campaigns use Feed posts, Stories and Reels. Meta recommends 4:5 (1440×1800) for feed images and 9:16 (1080×1920) for feed and Reels video. AIVideosUGC makes 6, 10, 15 or 30-second 9:16 clips and one square product image per job; crop the square still to 4:5 for the feed, run separate jobs when you want several carousel slides, then assemble them in Instagram. Keep key details inside the Reels safe area before publishing.

Upload your product shot along with a line about the setting: a serum bottle on a marble sink, sunglasses on a beach towel, a candle beside an open book. The result comes back to your account, private to you. Download it, write your caption, and add any text or stickers in Instagram, Canva or Ads Manager. For placement planning, a Reels demo keeps the action centered in 9:16, Stories can use three consecutive frames, and a Feed carousel can lead with the product, follow with scale, then show a detail. Generate each still separately and assemble the sequence in Instagram.

faq.q: How can I check an Instagram ad before publishing?
faq.a: Preview the asset in its intended placement and check that captions, reply areas, and profile controls do not cover key product details.

faq.q: Can I reuse a video across Instagram placements?
faq.a: Preview the downloaded file separately in each placement. Interface controls can cover different parts of the image, so check that the product and any added text stay clear.

faq.q: Can AIVideosUGC add my logo or a discount code?
faq.a: Add them yourself after download in Canva, CapCut or Ads Manager. Lettering drawn by AI can come out misspelled, so placing it yourself is safer.

faq.q: Will my product photos appear on Instagram or anywhere public?
faq.a: No. Everything you upload or create is kept private in your account. Nothing goes on Instagram unless you post it.

faq.q: How do I make a carousel from one product?
faq.a: Run separate square jobs for a front view, an in-hand view or a detail, then add the downloaded stills together as a carousel in Instagram.

faq.q: Should I choose a Reel or a feed post?
faq.a: Meta recommends 9:16 (1080×1920) video for Reels and the feed, and 4:5 (1440×1800) for a feed image. AIVideosUGC makes 9:16 clips and square stills to crop to 4:5; preview the crop and safe area in the intended placement.

faq.q: Do I need a model or a creator?
faq.a: No. The Reels clip and square still are generated from your product photo and a short description, so nothing has to be filmed. Add captions and stickers after download.

faq.q: Can I run these as paid ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloaded clips and stills are yours to use in Instagram ads, and they carry no AIVideosUGC watermark. You still need to follow Meta's current ad review rules.

overview.h2: Make a set that belongs together
overview.d: A consistent background and color palette can make a set of Instagram posts look like one campaign. AIVideosUGC returns one asset per job: make separate jobs for a front view, an in-hand view and a shelf view, crop the stills to Meta's recommended 4:5 (1440×1800), then publish them together as a carousel. Add a 9:16 Reel as its own job so the crop and safe area stay clear.

overview.h2: Design for Reels, Stories, and the feed separately
overview.d: Meta recommends 4:5 (1440×1800) feed images and 9:16 (1080×1920) video for the feed and Reels. AIVideosUGC makes 9:16 clips of 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds and square stills to crop to 4:5; use Meta's safe-zone checker for key messages before publishing.

overview.h2: Turn separate jobs into a useful carousel
overview.d: A carousel is assembled in Instagram after you create its slides. Run separate square jobs for a front view, an in-hand use moment, and a close detail; crop each to the Feed ratio you plan to use, then order the slides so the first frame introduces the item and later frames answer scale and use questions. Keep the product color and background family consistent across the set.

overview.h2: Give Reels and Stories their own framing
overview.d: Use a 9:16 job when the item needs to fill a phone screen. Keep faces, hands, and product details in the safe center because Instagram controls and captions occupy the edges. A square still can become a Feed image after cropping, but do not stretch it into a Reel. Preview every placement with the actual caption and stickers before publishing.

A strong Instagram ad shows a recognizable routine rather than a generic room. Show a hand applying cream before makeup, a sunscreen swipe before a walk, or a necklace being fastened before leaving. Name the action in the prompt, keep the product visible at the moment it is used, and add the final caption, price, and link in Instagram or Ads Manager after download.

overview.h2: Order carousel slides by shopper questions
overview.d: Lead with a complete front view, follow with an in-hand scale cue, and finish with one close detail or use moment. Keep each slide square until you crop the set for Feed. Add the caption, alt text, price, and link in Instagram or Ads Manager after reviewing the full carousel on a phone.

overview.h2: Map the scene to the Instagram placement
overview.d: Use a Reels demo for one spoken or visual action, a Stories sequence for three consecutive frames, and a Feed carousel for a main view followed by scale and detail. Generate each asset separately, keep the product consistent, then add captions, stickers and the final order in Instagram.

input_guide.h2: Give the model a source that survives the crop

items.d: Photograph the product at the angle you want shoppers to remember. Include handles, lids, straps, and other parts that should remain visible.
Say whether the scene is a bathroom shelf, cafe table, closet rail, or outdoor bench so the background supports the product.
Leave breathing room around the item. A centered product gives you more options when Instagram previews a square post or covers the edges with interface elements.
Use a clean 1:1 image as a feed post or one slide in a carousel, with the product easy to recognize.
Show the product in use in a 9:16 Reel, with the main action near the middle.
Add a close view of texture, hardware, packaging, or scale as another square carousel slide.

items.t: Routine Still — Serum at the Sink
items.d: Square still photo of an adult hand holding a serum bottle beside a bright sink while a single drop rests on the back of the other hand. Soft window light, natural beauty-photo detail, bottle and drop in sharp focus.

items.t: Try-On Still — Canvas Tote on Shoulder
items.d: Square still photo of an adult wearing a plain canvas tote over one shoulder at a cafe doorway, turning slightly so the front pocket is visible. Soft daylight, casual fashion styling, full tote in frame.

items.t: Product Detail Still — Single-Hole Phone Case
items.d: Square still photo of a plain dark silicone phone case with one small circular camera opening, held by an adult hand over a neutral surface. Keep the case edges, soft finish, and single opening clear in bright window light; no device or text.
Square still photo of adult hands lifting over-ear headphones from a plain box on a bright desk. Keep the headband and both earcups visible, with soft daylight and a clean top-down composition.
Type the product name, price, offer, and date in Instagram, Canva, CapCut, or Ads Manager instead of relying on generated lettering.
Add music or another permitted sound after download; AIVideosUGC does not add spoken explanation, music, or captions.
Open the finished Reel or Story preview and move added text away from profile controls, reply areas, and edge crops.
Use the caption to add details that do not belong inside the image, such as materials, sizing, or a shipping note.

Downloaded clips and stills carry no AIVideosUGC watermark and are yours to use in ads and posts, with the credit cost shown before each job.
